title: Control of jungle rice weed in annual crop fields - Vietnam

Header: Control of jungle rice weed in annual crop fields - Vietnam
Echinochloa colona Cỏlồng vực cạn, cỏnước mặn

Prevention: Purchase certified clean rice seed to avoid introduction through contamination.
Clean equipment and farm machinery after working in infested areas to prevent seeds being spread.
Control established populations near waterways by pulling or hoeing to prevent spread during flooding and storm events.
Before planting seed, prepare seed bed and wait for the first rain showers to promote weed germination then control by use of a post-emergence herbicide (glyphosate) when weeds are 2-3 weeks old.
Use upland crop rotation with paddy rice every year, if applicable.
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: upland rice, maize, soybean.
Annual grass, with fibrous, rather shallow roots.
Culms stout, erect with spreading open growth; often branching from base, 20-60cm tall.
Leaves: light green, sometimes with transverse purple bands, inflorescence erect or nodding, 5-15cm long.
No awns gives a less spikey appearance than
During the seedling stage, the stem of jungle rice weed has a reddish purple tinge while the rice crop stem is green.
Inspect fields every 2 weeks, in particular during and shortly after the wet season, and consider direct control when present.
Look out for the weed in wetlands and along waterways.
Water and storm events can spread seeds.
Direct Control: Hand-pull or hoe the weed before flowering.
Use butachlor (40-50 g a.i/ha) + propanil (450-600 g a.i/ha).
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
Use glyphosate (960-1200g a.i/ha) before planting when there is a heavy infestation of the weed.
The use of pre- and post- emergence herbicides refers to the emergence of the weed.
